title: Frizzled and the Fly Wing's Hairs

scenes.tts: Look at a fly wing. Each cell grows one hair, and every hair points toward the wing tip. A direction shared by the cells in the plane of a sheet is called planar cell polarity, or P C P. But no cell can see the whole sheet. So how does each cell know which way to point?
scenes.caption: Look at a fly wing. Each cell grows one hair, and every hair points toward the wing tip. A direction shared by the cells in the plane of a sheet is called planar cell polarity, or PCP. But no cell can see the whole sheet. So how does each cell know which way to point?
scenes.visual: A sheet of square cells, each with one blue hair arrow pointing to the tip at the right; labels base and tip. A PCP label appears; one cell is ringed and its hair swings round with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Look at a fly wing. Each cell grows one hair, and every hair points toward the wing tip. A direction shared by the cells in the plane of a sheet is called planar cell polarity, or PCP. But no cell can see the whole sheet. So how does each cell know which way to point?

scenes.tts: At the University of Virginia, in nineteen eighty-seven, Charles Vinson and Paul Adler made patches of cells that lack a gene called frizzled. The rest of each wing was normal. Would the normal cells beside a patch notice?
scenes.caption: At the University of Virginia, in 1987, Charles Vinson and Paul Adler made patches of cells that lack a gene called frizzled. The rest of each wing was normal. Would the normal cells beside a patch notice?
scenes.visual: The same sheet. Name tags for Vinson and Adler appear. A small patch of cells turns red, labelled no frizzled, and its hairs are not shown. The normal cells beside it are ringed with question marks.
scenes.narration: At the University of Virginia, in 1987, Charles Vinson and Paul Adler made patches of cells that lack a gene called frizzled. The rest of each wing was normal. Would the normal cells beside a patch notice?

scenes.tts: Normal cells on the tip side of a patch grew misdirected hairs. Normal cells on the other side did not. So a patch with no frizzled upset its normal neighbours, but on one side only.
scenes.caption: Normal cells on the tip side of a patch grew misdirected hairs. Normal cells on the other side did not. So a patch with no frizzled upset its normal neighbours, but on one side only.
scenes.visual: Small patch; tip-side neighbours get a yellow question mark (direction not shown) labelled misdirected; other side labelled normal.
scenes.narration: Normal cells on the tip side of a patch grew misdirected hairs. Normal cells on the other side did not. So a patch with no frizzled upset its normal neighbours, but on one side only.

scenes.tts: Two years later, Adler's laboratory cloned frizzled. It encodes a seven-pass membrane protein. It is the same Frizzled as in the Wnt receptor family, which is named for untidy hairs on a fly. This pathway does not use beta-catenin or T C F. In the wing, its output is the place where the cell builds the actin bundle that becomes its hair.
